result.summary:
WORKS. Anonymous S3 ListObjectsV2 gives a recursive listing WITH sizes (no HEAD needed), HEAD and Range requests work, and pxr opens the USDs. The recipe (stdlib for list/fetch/MDL, pxr for USD) builds a categorised catalogue (/.../assets3d/catalogue.json, 1.1 MB, ~1,900 assets in 16 categories) plus all 161 NVIDIA/Materials/Base .mdl texture sets, and opens 10-11 representative assets.

KEY FINDINGS
1. The three folders named in the task are only part of it. NVIDIA/Assets/Vegetation (44 trees, 37 shrub/grass, 17 tropical, 15 rocks, 10 debris/leaves) is there, but ArchVis is almost all INTERIOR furniture. The outdoor gold mine is NVIDIA/dsready_content/nv_content/{common_assets,usa/country_assets} (175,822 objects, 116 GB; Rivermark carries a 11.7 GB subset of it): 79 full-size trees, 19 shrubs, 26 grass clumps, ~60 vehicles, 130 lamp posts, 66 utility poles, 134 fences/walls, 188 signs, hydrants, mailboxes, bus stops, bins, 20 generic 12-95 m buildings, etc.
2. UNITS DIFFER: NVIDIA/Assets/{Vegetation,ArchVis,DigitalTwin} are centimetres (metersPerUnit 0.01); DSReady and Rivermark are metres (1.0), except DSReady bldgs_01_distant (0.01). All Z-up. USD references do not convert units, so scale 0.01 for cm assets (recipe.place() does this and tested: Douglas_Fir 602 cm -> 6.03 m).
3. NOT in the mirror: single-family houses (nearest: kasa_house_01..03 = 12x33x6.6 m townhome blocks, wyatt_house 78x20x19 m, typical_building_*/bldg_gen_* 9-95 m mid-rise), crops (no corn/wheat/soy), barns/silos/tractors, playground equipment (only a child's Playhouse.usd, 27.6 MB), ordinary passenger cars beyond tri/auto_01 (4.85x2.04x1.42 m), tri/police_01, tri/security_01, honey/* codename cars/trucks and the 4.0 m ncap_soft_car target. Houses/roofs must stay procedural, dressed with Base materials.
4. Materials: 161 Base .mdl (OmniPBR, 2K PNG albedo+ORM+normal, 8-bit RGB); ground/roof/wall set complete (Asphalt, Dirt, Grass_Cut/Countryside/Winter, Gravel, Pea_Gravel, Sand, Soil_Rocky, Leaves, Mulch, Water, Roof_Tiles, Shingles_01, Brick_Wall_Red/Brown, Stucco, Concrete_*, Timber_Cladding, Metal_Seamed_Roof, Chain_Link_Fence...). Each textured material costs 8-30 MB (3 PNG at 2048^2).
5. Rivermark = NVIDIA DRIVE-Sim 'Rivermark Plaza' (Santa Clara, CA) road/plaza scene, only 1.12 x 0.83 km, 11.7 GB, 'Limited Use Content' licence (no modifications): useless as the large scene itself, but a ready closure of ~2,000 outdoor props. It is not our landscape.
6. Heavy: Isaac Vegetation trees are 0.8-82 MB per root file (+14-18 MB shared textures; Red_Maple closure 32.7 MB), so km-scale forests need few species + instancing. Typical DSReady _inst closures: hydrant 6 MB, lamp 3 MB, car target 10 MB, building 17 MB.

PATHS / NAMING (rel = path under https://omniverse-content-production.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/Assets/Isaac/5.1/ ; recipe.url(rel) percent-encodes). Listing: GET https://omniverse-content-production.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=Assets/Isaac/5.1/<prefix>&max-keys=1000 (+continuation-token); ~10k keys/s, ~300 B XML per key. NEVER list NVIDIA/dsready_content/ whole (175k keys, 113 s, ~55 MB XML): list sub-trees, or use NVIDIA/dsready_content/file_list.txt (10.9 MB, paths only, no sizes). Same for Isaac/Environments/Outdoor/Rivermark/dsready_content/file_list.txt (2 MB). drone_scene.nucleus.list_dir/url work unchanged.

FILE-LAYOUT RULES
* Isaac Vegetation / ArchVis / DigitalTwin: one self-contained .usd (geometry inside) + ./materials/<Name>.mdl + ./materials/textures/*.png (shared by many assets of the folder; Vegetation Rocks use ./textures/*.jpg + Kit's OmniPBR.mdl). cm units, Z up, NOT instanceable (instanceable_prims=0; rocks 1) -> set instanceable=True on the referencing prim or use PointInstancer.
* DSReady: folder <name>/ with <name>.usd (wrapper: sublayer <name>_base.usd, authoring prim <name>_inst [instanceable=true] and a Tagging/ThumbRig reference), <name>_inst.usd (sublayer <name>_inst_base.usd = geometry+Looks), textures in ./materials/textures or ../shared_textures. Metres, Z up, defaultPrim /RootNode. PREFER <name>_inst.usd as the entry point: same geometry, closure 2-5x smaller (hydrant 6.2 vs 30.8 MB, car target 10.4 vs 33.5, building 16.6 vs 25.4, picket fence 16.4 vs 39.6) because the wrapper drags in nv_core thumbnail rigs, studio_lights.usd (1.4 MB) + cotton/HDRI images (~4 MB) and physics materials. _inst root is not itself instanceable: mark the referencing prim. The wrapper may add a transform (fence_picket_1m: wrapper 0.1 x 2.32 x 1.13 m, _inst 2.32 x 0.1 x 1.13 m).
* Some refs are dead and harmless: wrapper ./materials/textures/*.png that 404 (real ones in common_assets/shared_textures), Windows sublayers 'D:/P4_OV/.../*_prototypes.usd' (veg_tree_pine_yellow_01, veg_shrub_hedge_*), thumbnail-rig SimPBR.mdl. The recipe skips drive paths; nucleus.mirror_usd treats 404 as skippable.
* Vehicles: vehicles/<make>/<model>/<year>/main.usd (+ instance/*.usd parts, 40-50 MB of layers for a car). Skyline blocks bldgs_02_distant/Building_NNN.usd are world-positioned city blocks (Building_109: 8352 x 10911 m extent!), bldgs_01_distant are 0.01-unit single blocks (Building_178 60.4x32.9x5.7 m).

WORKS. Overture is reachable via S3 only through plain HTTPS range requests (requests + the proxy); no whole-file downloads needed. Method: (1) list release/ with S3 ListObjectsV2 (delimiter=/) to get the latest release; (2) per type, read the last 16 KB of every parquet file and parse the GeoParquet 'geo' JSON metadata, which holds the file-level bbox (index of all 7 layers = 19 MB of requests, 2-4 s per type with 32 threads, cached as JSON); (3) for the 1-4 candidate files fetch the footer (0.15-2 MB), prune row groups with bbox.xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax statistics, then read in two phases: first only the small bbox column of surviving row groups, then geometry and other heavy columns only for row groups that still contain intersecting rows. Output is a pyarrow.Table (WKB geometry, EPSG:4326) plus helpers to_shapely, clip_to_bbox, to_local_metres (UTM), estimate_cost (dry run), bbox_around.

Counts in the 4x3 km Ames test box (release 2026-09-23.1): building 3600 (2139 have height = 59%, 142 num_floors, 3 roof_shape, 1833 class, 1842 subtype; heights 0.14-18.5 m, median 4.6 m; ~85 ha of footprints); building_part 0; transportation/segment 1599 (290 km: footway 510, service 445, residential 432, cycleway 76, secondary 49, path 23, primary 22, tertiary 22, motorway 6; 3 rail segments of 14-29 km); base/water 60 (35 stream lines, 18 ponds, 3 swimming pools, reservoirs); base/land_use 206 (residential 73, managed 44, recreation 26, agriculture 21, developed 17, park 8); base/land_cover 50 (ESA WorldCover vector polygons: shrub 18, forest 15, barren 8, crop 5, urban 4); base/land 253 of which 220 are individual tree POINTS (subtype=tree, class=tree, from OSM natural=tree), 20 woods, 6 wetland, 3 scrub, 1 tree_row; base/infrastructure 1081 (989 points: crossings 488, kerbs 346, bus stops 50, fire hydrants 22, traffic signals 14; plus 66 polygons e.g. parking, 26 lines, 14 bridges, 12 power).

All parquet are zstd, 16k-50k rows per row group, written by parquet-cpp-arrow 17, NO parquet page index (so the smallest readable unit is a row group, typically 3-13 MB for the geometry-heavy layers).
- Parquet footer is 0.15-2.0 MB per file (building 0.7-1.4 MB, segment 2.0 MB). Last 8 bytes = footer length + 'PAR1'.
- Geo metadata (key 'geo', GeoParquet 1.1.0, encoding WKB, covering.bbox -> bbox.xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax) is found in the last 16 KB of the file and contains the whole-file bbox [w,s,e,n]; verified for all 1152 files scanned (none missing). Files are NOT sorted by longitude but along a space-filling curve, and file bboxes can be large (e.g. building part-00044 covers lon -104.9..-93.5, lat 38.6..42.5) so candidate files are found by file bbox, then row groups by stats.

- water: subtype/class (stream 35, pond 18, human_made/swimming_pool 3, water 2, reservoir/basin 2), is_salt, is_intermittent, level, names; geometry 26 polygons + 34 lines (streams are lines).
- land_use: subtype (residential, managed, recreation, agriculture, developed, park, horticulture, education), class (residential, grass, commercial, pitch, farmland, playground, park, farmyard), surface (recreation_paved, concrete, recreation_grass), names; polygons.
- land_cover: subtype (barren, crop, forest, grass, shrub, snow, urban, water, wetland, mangrove, moss) and cartography struct {prominence, min_zoom, max_zoom, sort_key}. MULTI-LEVEL PYRAMID: rows with max_zoom 7 are continent-scale generalised polygons (up to 8 million km2, 14k-61k vertices) overlapping the real ones; rows with min_zoom 8 / max_zoom 15 are the 10 m ESA WorldCover polygons. recipe.read_bbox drops max_zoom<15 by default (finest_only=True); without this the clipped land-cover area in the box is 26.7 km2 for a 12 km2 box.
- land: subtype (tree 221, forest 20, wetland 6, shrub 3, grass 1, sand 1, land 1), class (tree 220, wood 20, wetland 6, scrub 3, tree_row 1, grassland, sand, land), surface, elevation, names; 220 Points (trees), 32 polygons, 1 line.
- infrastructure: subtype (transportation 530, barrier 357, transit 110, pedestrian 23, emergency 22, bridge 14, power 12, waste_management 6), class (crossing, kerb, parking, bus_stop, fire_hydrant, stop, traffic_signals, bridge ...), surface, height (0 set), level, names; points mostly.
- Every table has sources: list of {property, dataset, license, record_id, update_time, confidence, ...}. No 'tree' or 'vegetation' type exists in Overture; trees are only OSM natural=tree points under base/land. No building texture/photo data. Overture does not give lane counts or road width in Ames.

HOW TO CALL: from recipe import read_bbox, to_shapely, clip_to_bbox, to_local_metres, estimate_cost, bbox_around, ByteCounter, DEFAULT_COLUMNS. tbl = read_bbox('building', (w,s,e,n), columns=None|list|'all', cache_dir=..., counter=ByteCounter(), cache_result=False). geoms = to_shapely(tbl); gm, epsg = to_local_metres(geoms, lon0, lat0) gives a UTM-based metric frame centred on lon0/lat0 (Ames: EPSG:32615). Default columns omit the heavy 'sources' and 'connectors'; add 'sources' to get the per-record licence. Caches live in ./cache (index_<rel>_<type>.json, footer_*.bin, tables/*.parquet); override with env OVERTURE_CACHE. Run `python recipe.py [--summary] [--fresh]`.

BOX SIZE SCALING (dry-run estimate_cost, compressed data bytes, 7 layers): 4x3 km 93 MB; 10x10 km 105 MB; 20x20 km 114 MB. Per layer for 4x3 km (before the two-phase optimisation): building 2.9, segment 5.6, water 24.8 (geometry of large water polygons dominates), land_use 9.3, land_cover 36.0 (now 13.3 after skipping empty/coarse row groups), land 3.6, infrastructure 10.9 MB. Several row groups are shared when the box grows, so a very large scene of tens of km costs only a few extra row groups per layer.

## Bucket layout (https://dataforgood-fb-data.s3.amazonaws.com/<key>; list with ?list-type=2&prefix=...)
v1 (prefix forests/v1/alsgedi_global_v6_float/):
- chm/<9-digit quadkey>.tif: uint8 metres, 65536x65536 px, EPSG:3857, deflate + horizontal predictor. ONE-ROW STRIPS, not tiled, NO overviews, tile ~160-260 MB. Nodata tag is None.
- msk/<qk>.tif.msk: 65536^2 uint8 deflate, no georef, same pixel grid as the tif, ~6 MB. Values 0/255. POLARITY IS THE OPPOSITE of the bucket readme.
  - 255 = flagged/no data, and the CHM is 0 there. Evidence: 99.99% of the Ames window is 0 while CHM has data; an all-255 Arctic tile has CHM == 0 everywhere; the 255 fraction over whole tiles is 0.03% (Ames), 12-28% (other tiles).
  - 0 = valid.
  - If the .msk is ever placed next to the .tif, GDAL would auto-apply it with the inverse meaning. Keep them separate.
- metadata/<qk>.geojson: polygons with property acq_date, 44 MB for the Ames tile. Not needed, because a cheap raster exists (next item).
- CHM_acquisition_date.tif (2 GB, EPSG:4326, 0.01 deg, float32, uncompressed 1-row strips, 36001x13985): windowed read of a few KB. Value = year-2000 as a decimal fraction, e.g. 18.667 = 2018.67 (Aug 2018). 0 = none.
- tiles.geojson (15 MB; properties.tile = quadkey; polygons are really EPSG:4326 although the readme says 3857).
- readme: forests/v1/readme.txt. Downsampled 1/4000 deg derivatives: alsgedi_global_v6_float_epsg4326_v3_10deg/meta_chm_lat=..._lon=..._{avg,median,stdev,p95,cover,count,cover5m,count5m}.tif (uint16 cm, nodata 65535).
v2 (prefix forests/v2/global/dinov3_global_chm_v2_ml3/):
- chm/<10-digit quadkey>.tif: uint8 metres, 32768x32768 px, EPSG:3857, 512x512 tiles, deflate, no predictor, overviews [2,4,8,16,32,64]. A true COG: ~55 MB for the Ames tile, 8.4 KB per 512 tile.
  - No nodata tag; instead an INTERNAL per-dataset mask (mask_flag per_dataset, stored as IFD 1). Read it with ds.read_masks(1). Only 0.01% of the Ames window is masked.
  - Water and bare ground are valid 0 m.
- metadata/<qk>.geojson: polygons with acq_date, 11-14 MB per tile for Ames. The recipe downloads and caches it, then intersects with the bbox via shapely.

## Tile maths
- Quadkey digit = (x bit) + 2*(y bit) at each zoom; tile -> quadkey is in the recipe (lonlat_to_tile, tile_to_quadkey, quadkeys_for_bbox).
- Global pixel col = floor((x_merc + 20037508.342789244)/1.1943285668550503); row = floor((20037508.342789244 - y_merc)/1.19432856685505).
- Tile origin px = tx*tp, ty*tp with tp = 65536 (v1) or 32768 (v2).
- Tile edges are 58-78 km apart for v1 and 29-39 km for v2 at mid latitudes.
## Recipe API (recipe.py; run as `python -I recipe.py [v1|v2] [W S E N]`)
- quadkeys_for_bbox(bbox, version), tile_url(qk, version), tile_exists(url).
- read_chm(bbox, version="v2", use_cloud_mask=True) returns Chm.
  - Chm.data is uint8 metres with 255 = nodata (missing tile, v1 mask, v2 internal mask). Chm.col0/row0 is the global zoom-17 pixel offset; Chm.transform is an Affine in EPSG:3857.
  - Helpers: height_m() (float32 with NaN), ground_pixel_m(), pix_to_lonlat(), save_geotiff().
- acquisition_info(bbox, version): v1 reads the date raster (cheap); v2 downloads the metadata geojson.
- detect_trees(chm, min_height=3.0, sigma_m=1.0, window_frac=0.55, crown_frac=0.5, max_crown_d=25, block=2048) returns a numpy structured array with fields lon, lat, x_m, y_m, height_m, crown_diam_m.
  - x_m/y_m are east/north metres in an azimuthal-equidistant frame centred on the bbox centre, or on origin_lonlat if given.
- trees_to_csv(trees, path).
- worldcover_class_areas(bbox, year=2021): reads s3://esa-worldcover (https://esa-worldcover.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/v200/2021/map/ESA_WorldCover_10m_2021_v200_N42W096_Map.tif; 3x3 deg COG tiles, reachable here).
## Detection algorithm
1. nodata -> 0, then Gaussian smoothing with sigma 1 m (converted to px with the true ground pixel size).
2. Local maxima of the smoothed CHM with a height-dependent square window (side = 0.55 * (1.2 + 0.4*h) m, >= 3 px, odd). One maximum_filter per unique window size, so it is fast. Plateau ties are merged by label + centre of mass.
3. Tree height = max raw CHM in the 3x3 around the top; trees below min_height are dropped.
4. Crowns: marker-controlled watershed (scipy.ndimage.watershed_ift on the inverted smoothed CHM). Crown = basin pixels with h >= 0.5*treetop height and within an allometric max radius; crown_diam = 2*sqrt(area/pi).
- Results are fairly insensitive to parameters. n trees varies only 10.1k-13.3k over sigma 0.7-1.5 m and window_frac 0.35-0.8 (v2, Ames).
## Numbers for the test area (v2 unless stated)
- Window: 3263 rows x 4662 cols.
- Height histogram of trees (3-6, 6-9, 9-12, 12-15, 15-20, 20+ m): 1424, 1922, 1784, 1751, 3013, 1966. Tree height percentiles p5/25/50/75/95/max: 4/8/13/18/24/32 m.
- v1 histogram (3-6, 6-9, 9-12, 12-15, 15-20, 20-25, 25+): 1288, 1368, 1355, 1303, 1583, 404, 9.
- Crown diameter p5/50/95: 3.3/8.3/16.6 m (v2); 3.5/8.0/15.0 m (v1).
- Canopy area (km2) at thresholds >=1/2/3/5/10/15/20 m: v1 2.71/2.40/2.18/1.84/1.12/0.46/0.05; v2 2.86/2.70/2.58/2.33/1.71/1.00/0.37.
- Mean |dh| between adjacent rows across the tile seam (lat ~42.03): v2 1.54 m, v1 0.64 m, versus ~0.15 m inside a tile.
- Match between detections: 33% of v1 trees have a v2 tree within 3 m (66% within 5 m).
- WorldCover classes, by share of area: tree 27.4%, crop 30.9%, built-up 24.7%, grass 16.8%.
  - Share of 10 m pixels with CHM >=3 m, v1/v2: tree 56%/63%, grass 6%/9%, built-up 6%/9%, crop 2%/2%.
  - Mean height in the built-up class is 0.5/0.8 m, so roofs are not mapped as canopy.
## Gotchas
- Mercator pixel is 1.194 m but only 0.887 m on the ground at 42N. Always use ground size = 1.19433*cos(lat) for metric work; the recipe does.
- Heights are integer metres (1 m quantisation) and the CHM is a smooth model output, not lidar. Crowns merge, so tree counts are a lower bound.
  - Crown circles cover only ~36% of the >=3 m canopy area (insensitive to crown_frac and max_crown_d). For visually dense forest in a scene, top up with extra trees sampled from the CHM.
  - Detection density is ~46 trees per canopy-hectare.
- Tiles are predicted independently (different imagery dates). There is a step along the seam and a faint thin streak; mind this at the seam lat ~42.03 in the test box. Trees near the window edge can have truncated crowns, so read with a margin.
- The seam test could not reproduce a row artifact over farmland (all zeros), but the column seam at the large-test tile edge was clean.

result.summary:
Both sources work from this machine with no STAC API, using only S3 HTTPS (anonymous) and GDAL /vsicurl/.
(1) WorldCover: 3x3 deg COG tiles, EPSG:4326, uint8, nodata 0. A 4x3 km window is ~0.16 MB and takes ~1.2 s. The recipe mosaics several tiles on the global 1/12000 deg grid. Ocean tiles do not exist in the bucket (404) and are filled with 0. v200/2021 and v100/2020 both work.
(2) Sentinel-2: 46 products exist for Jun-Aug 2026 on MGRS tile 15TVG (48 for Jun-Aug 2025). Data is in the bucket through at least Oct 2026. Discovery uses plain S3 ListObjectsV2 (delimiter '/'), then each product's ~22 kB STAC item json (<pid>.json) for tile-wide cloud metadata. The recipe also reads the 20 m SCL window of the bbox for every candidate (~0.08 MB each) to get the LOCAL cloud/shadow fraction. Tile-wide eo:cloud_cover is a poor proxy: in the mosaic test a scene with 13.9 % tile cloud was fully clear over the bbox.
Pick: S2C_15TVG_20260808_0_L2A (2026-08-08, baseline 05.12, tile cloud 0.02 %, local cloud/shadow/nodata 0.00 %, median NDVI 0.78 over vegetation pixels = peak leaf-on). Six scenes were fully clear locally, and the one with the highest NDVI wins the tie-break.
RGB comes from B04/B03/B02 reflectance (DN/10000, NOT minus 0.1) -> clip(2.5*refl) -> sRGB OETF, on a UTM 10 m grid (EPSG:32615, 417x293 px, aligned with the S2 pixel grid, so no resampling).
Also tested: a 29x17 km bbox straddling the lon -93.0 boundary (WorldCover tiles N42W096|N42W093 and S2 tiles 15TWG|15TVG), run at 40 m through COG overviews, gave a seamless mosaic for 14 MB. MGRS ids were checked for Sydney (56HLH), Zurich (32TMT), London (30UXC), Ames (15TVG) and Munich (32UPU), including the S hemisphere and an even UTM zone.

Brightness mapping (reflectance_to_srgb): lin = clip(gain*refl, 0, 1) with gain 2.5 (fixed), then the sRGB transfer function (12.92x for lin <= 0.0031308, else 1.055*lin^(1/2.4)-0.055), x255, uint8; nodata (any band DN 0) -> RGB 0. Keep the gain constant across all tiles of a scene for consistent brightness. It looks natural but slightly hazy; raise contrast (e.g. gain 3) or darken for albedo textures as needed. If the texture is meant as albedo under the sim's own lighting, note it is already display-referred (bright roofs ~200).
Metric grid: make_grid(bbox, res) -> UTM zone of the bbox centre (EPSG:32615 for the test), snapped outward to multiples of res (10/20/40 m are aligned with all S2 tiles in any UTM zone; 60/80 m are not for every tile and then use a slower WarpedVRT path), dict(crs, epsg, transform, width, height, res, bounds). A lon/lat bbox becomes a slightly rotated quadrilateral, so the rectangle is a bit larger than the box.
Reading: _read_on_grid() uses a plain windowed read (fast path, same CRS + aligned + integer ratio k >= 1: k=2,4,8,16 hit the COG overviews, so coarse previews of big areas are cheap, 40 m is ~4x cheaper than 10 m) and otherwise WarpedVRT (bilinear for imagery, nearest for classes; it does NOT use overviews and reads full-res blocks). Window outside the tile -> 0.
Cost per band: a 4.2x2.9 km window at 10 m touches ~4 of the 1024x1024 blocks = ~2.8 MB per band, so RGB via B04+B03+B02 ~8.3 MB, via TCI (read_s2_rgb mode='tci') ~4.1 MB; roughly 0.7 MB per band per 10x10 km block at 10 m. SCL window ~0.08 MB. A 29x17 km multi-tile mosaic at 40 m cost 14 MB total including all candidate ranking.

result.problems:
Nothing blocking. Things that behaved unexpectedly or are limitations:
- STAC raster:bands offset (-0.1) for baseline >= 04.00 does not match the data: the COG DNs carry no +1000 offset (reflectance = DN/10000). I verified this empirically on water pixels across baselines 03.01 to 05.12 and against ESA's TCI; I could not read Element84's documentation from here to confirm the intended semantics, so the recipe hard-codes S2_REFL_OFFSET = 0.0.
- tileinfo_metadata.json cloudyPixelPercentage is unreliable (0.0 when eo:cloud_cover was 15 %); use the product json (eo:cloud_cover) and, better, the local SCL fraction.
- Tile-wide cloud cover is a poor proxy for a small bbox, so the recipe reads SCL per candidate (0.08 MB each).
- WarpedVRT reads full-res blocks and never uses COG overviews (80 m read cost the same 2.8 MB as 10 m); the fast direct-window path with out_shape is needed for cheap coarse reads, and it only applies on aligned grids with res in {10, 20, 40} m for same-zone tiles.
- Multi-tile mosaics use different dates, so a mild brightness seam is visible; bboxes spanning two UTM zones were not tested (the code reprojects through WarpedVRT but is untested).
- 10 m Sentinel-2 is coarse for a drone scene (houses are 1-3 px): treat it as base albedo/colour map and use WorldCover classes plus OSM footprints for structure. WorldCover class 50 'built-up' includes yards/driveways at 10 m.
- The loopback byte counter and /proc/net/dev were too noisy for accounting; the DownloadMeter in the recipe parses GDAL CPL_DEBUG 'Downloading a-b' lines and requests content length instead (accurate to the request level).
- WorldCover tile files are 65 MB for this region and the macrotile zips are many GB; the recipe only ever range-reads windows.
- Not tested: antimeridian crossing, polar (>84 N / <60 S) areas where WorldCover has no coverage, UTM zone-boundary mosaics.

result.summary:
All four sources work from this machine over S3 and were tested. The recipe `get_height_grid(bbox_lonlat, spacing_m)` returns a float32 height grid in metres with row 0 at the north edge. The grid is in a local transverse-mercator CRS centred on the bbox, so x and y are metres east and north of the scene centre. It tries 3dep_1m, then 3dep_13, then cop30, then terrarium. It takes the first source that covers at least 99.5% of the cells. Missing cells are filled from the next source after a median vertical-offset match, and anything left is filled by nearest-neighbour interpolation.

The TNM API (tnmaccess.nationalmap.gov) is blocked from this machine (curl: "CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403", a proxy policy denial). It is not needed. 1 m tiles are located entirely from files in the prd-tnm bucket. FESM_1m.gpkg holds the project footprints and is read with HTTP range requests through an apsw VFS, which takes about 2 to 3 s and 2.5 MB of a 1.9 GB file. Each project's 0_file_download_links.txt, cached on disk, gives its tile URLs. Tile names encode UTM zone, x and y, so the covering tiles are computed directly.

For the test area, FESM returned exactly one project, IA_NorthCentral_2020_D20, and the single tile USGS_1M_15_x44y466_...tif covers the whole bbox.

Elevation agreement on the test area at 2 m, against the 3DEP 1 m bare-earth result:

| Source | Bias (m) | RMSE (m) | p95 abs diff (m) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3dep_13 | -0.01 | 0.21 | 0.43 | |
| terrarium | -0.04 | 0.32 | 0.49 | In the US it is built from 3DEP, so it agrees closely |
| cop30 | +1.22 | 3.58 | 8.48 | It is a DSM, so trees and buildings stand out |

Further tests all passed:
- A 13 x 11 km box at 5 m.
- A 16.7 x 11 km box straddling the UTM 15/16 boundary, where tiles exist in both zones and are de-duplicated.
- A box crossing a 1-degree tile corner (4 tiles of 3dep_13).
- A coastal box (Galveston), where 1 m is only 70% valid and 3dep_13 fills the water.
- Non-US boxes (Zurich, Sydney) falling back to Copernicus.
- Terrarium outside the US (Zurich).

For a large scene, 1 m data can be used at any spacing without downloading whole tiles (a 1 m tile is 290 MB). The recipe reads the matching internal overview of each tile, so a 5 m grid reads the 4 m overview. This matches full-resolution averaging to 0.047 m RMSE and uses about 4x less data than reading full resolution.

## Files
- recipe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-vla-datagen/39bfe37a-c345-5663-b8fb-e785cd7a1b70/scratchpad/world_scout/elevation/recipe.py
- test outputs: .../elevation/out/height.npy, height.tif, hillshade.png (2072x1445 px at 2 m; the hillshade looks right, with city streets and a creek valley)
- cache of link lists: .../elevation/cache/links_<project>.json
- Run: `$PY -I recipe.py [--bbox W S E N] [--spacing 2] [--large] [--compare]`. `--large` uses a 13x11 km box, `--compare` reads each source separately and prints the stats and differences.
- Extra pip install: none. apsw 3.53.4.0 was already in the venv. On the user's PC run `pip install apsw`; without it the recipe logs a warning and skips 3dep_1m.

## Recipe API (all with docstrings)
- `get_height_grid(bbox, spacing=2.0, crs="local_tm"|"utm"|<any CRS>, sources=("3dep_1m","3dep_13","cop30","terrarium"), min_coverage=0.995, fill_gaps=True, cache_dir=None, verbose=False)` returns a dict:
  - `height` (ny, nx) float32 in metres; row 0 is north; no NaN after fill_gaps.
  - `transform` (Affine), `crs` (rasterio CRS), `x` and `y` (cell-centre coordinates), `bounds`, `spacing`, `origin_lonlat`.
  - `source_map` (uint8 index into `source_names`; 255 means interpolated), `source_names`.
  - `info` (per-source seconds, bytes, valid_fraction, project and tile names), plus `seconds` and `bytes`.
- Helpers: `local_crs`, `local_bounds`, `make_grid`, `fesm_projects`, `find_3dep_1m_tiles`, `find_3dep_13_tiles`, `find_cop30_tiles`, `read_geotiffs_onto_grid`, `read_terrarium_onto_grid`, `read_source`, `save_geotiff`, `hillshade`.
- Switch `USE_OVERVIEWS` (module level, default True) controls the overview optimisation.
- Cache directory: `cache_dir` argument, else env `WORLD_ELEVATION_CACHE`, else `~/.cache/world_elevation`. Link lists expire after 14 days.

## Local CRS and grid
- Default `local_tm`: `+proj=tmerc +lat_0=<bbox centre lat> +lon_0=<bbox centre lon> +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=GRS80 +units=m`. (0,0) is the bbox centre and the axes are metres east and north. Scale error is below 1e-5 within 30 km.
- `crs="utm"` gives EPSG:326xx or 327xx for the centre zone.
- Horizontal datum differences (NAD83 vs WGS84, about 1 m) are ignored (ballpark transform).
- Grid: the envelope of the densified lon/lat bbox in the local CRS, snapped outward to a multiple of the spacing. Samples are cell centres.
- Test area at 2 m: 2072 x 1445 cells, x from -2072 to 2072 m and y from -1444 to 1446 m, centre lon/lat (-93.69, 42.025).

## 1. USGS 3DEP 1 m (prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com, anonymous S3)
- Projects: `StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/Projects/<project>/`. There are 968 project prefixes. Each holds `0_file_download_links.txt` (full tile URLs), `TIFF/`, `browse/` and `metadata/`.
- Link file availability: 39 of 40 random projects had it. MI_25County_AlleganCo_2015 did not, so the recipe falls back to a paged ListObjectsV2 of `<project>/TIFF/`.
- Tile naming: `TIFF/USGS_1M_<utmzone>_x<xx>y<yyy>_<project>.tif`. Older projects use `USGS_one_meter_x..y.._<project>.tif` or `USGS_1m_x..y..` with no zone, and the recipe regex handles all three.
  - x = left easting / 10000 and y = TOP northing / 10000, in NAD83 UTM (verified: x44y466 spans E 439994..450006, N 4649994..4660006).
  - Test tile: `https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/Projects/IA_NorthCentral_2020_D20/TIFF/USGS_1M_15_x44y466_IA_NorthCentral_2020_D20.tif`
  - Tiles that cross a UTM zone boundary are delivered in both zones, and the recipe reads each ground area only once.
- Tile format: 10012 x 10012 px (10 km plus a 6 px buffer each side), 1.0 m pixels, EPSG:26915 (NAD83 / UTM 15N), float32, nodata -999999, LZW, 512x512 tiled, internal overviews 2/4/8/16/32. The test tile is 289,987,339 bytes.
- Vertical: metres, NAVD88 (geoid model is project specific). Bare-earth DTM, hydro-flattened, produced from lidar. Seamless within a project but not necessarily across projects.
- Test-tile metadata: tile pubdate 2022-12-09, FESM pub_date 2022-12-18, lidar collected 2020-04-04 to 2020-12-05.
- Coverage: only where 3DEP lidar exists (large parts of CONUS, some AK and HI), not everywhere. Outside it, FESM returns no project (Zurich and Sydney returned none).
- Locating tiles without the TNM API:
  - `.../StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/FullExtentSpatialMetadata/FESM_1m.gpkg`: 1,928,802,304 bytes, GeoPackage, layer `fesm_1m`, MULTIPOLYGON in EPSG:4269, 934 project rows.
  - Fields: fid, geometry, project, project_id, pub_date, product_link, metadata_link. `rtree_fesm_1m_geometry` (id, minx, maxx, miny, maxy) is the R-tree.
  - The file was last modified on the day of testing, so it is updated frequently. The bucket also contains a stale `FESM_1m.gpkg-journal`. The apsw VFS `xAccess` returns False for `-journal`, `-wal` and `-shm` so SQLite never tries to roll it back.
  - GeoPackage geometry blob: 8-byte header plus envelope (size from the flags bits 1-3), then WKB. The recipe strips it and uses `shapely.from_wkb` plus an intersects test, since R-tree boxes are only envelopes.
  - Projects are sorted by pub_date descending; newer projects win and older ones only fill gaps.
  - Also in that folder: `10_km_cell_grid.gpkg` (51 MB, not used).
- Mixing projects: the project gap fill in the 3dep_1m source does not apply an offset. Offsets are matched only when falling back to other sources.

## 2. USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second seamless
- Tile: `https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/13/TIFF/current/n43w094/USGS_13_n43w094.tif`, 415,821,732 bytes, last modified 2022-12-20. Sibling files in the folder are `.xml`, `.jpg` and `.gpkg`.
- Naming: n<ceil lat>w<abs lon of west edge, 3 digits>, i.e. the NW corner. n43w094 covers lat 42..43 and lon -94..-93. The recipe confirms existence with one tiny prefix listing per tile.
- Format: 10812 x 10812 px (1 degree plus 6 px buffer), pixel 1/10800 degree (9.259e-05 deg, about 10 m x 8 m at 42N), EPSG:4269 (NAD83 geographic), float32, nodata -999999, LZW, 512 blocks, overviews 2/4/8/16/32. Vertical NAVD88 metres, bare earth.
- It uses the best available source, including lidar, so over Ames it matches the 1 m data (RMSE 0.2 m).
- Coverage: CONUS and some neighbouring areas. There was no tile for Zurich or Sydney.

## 3. Copernicus DEM GLO-30
- Tile: `https://copernicus-dem-30m.s3.amazonaws.com/Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N42_00_W094_00_DEM/Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N42_00_W094_00_DEM.tif`. Naming uses the SW corner: `{N|S}{abs lat:02d}_00_{E|W}{abs lon:03d}_00`.
- Format: 3600 x 3600 px, EPSG:4326, 1/3600 degree (0.000278 deg; lon spacing coarser at high latitude), float32, no nodata value (ocean is 0), COG with 1024 blocks and overviews 2/4/8, AREA_OR_POINT=Point.
- Vertical: EGM2008 orthometric, metres. It is a DSM (radar surface including trees and buildings). Global coverage; missing ocean tiles return 404 and are skipped.
- Over the test area it is about +1.2 m biased with 3.6 m RMSE against the bare-earth lidar.
- Worked for Zurich and Sydney (S34_00_E151 tile). The Sydney min of -6.3 m comes from the data, not the recipe.
- License: Copernicus DEM licence; free use with attribution to the Copernicus programme / ESA / DLR / Airbus.

## 4. AWS Terrain Tiles (elevation-tiles-prod.s3.amazonaws.com)
- Top-level prefixes: docs/, geotiff/, lib/, logs/, normal/, skadi/, terrarium/, v2/.
- `terrarium/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`: 256x256 RGB PNG, Web Mercator, XYZ scheme, z up to 15. height_m = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768. A tile is about 90 KB.
- z15 pixel is 4.777 m at the equator, about 3.55 m at 42N. Real detail in the US is the 3DEP data (about 10 m), mixed with SRTM and others elsewhere. The recipe picks the smallest zoom (max 15) whose pixel is at most the spacing.
- `geotiff/{z}/{x}/{y}.tif`: 512x512 float32 EPSG:3857, nodata -3.4e38, deflate. It exists only up to z14; z15 returns 404. Same data as terrarium, larger files.
- `normal/` holds normal-map PNGs. `skadi/` holds SRTM 1 arc-second HGT; I saw the prefix but did not test it.
- Vertical datum is mixed (3DEP NAVD88 in the US). In Zurich terrarium was -2.4 m biased with 4.4 m RMSE against cop30, which is expected since they are different surface products.
- License: depends on the source datasets (3DEP is public domain; SRTM and others are attribution-requiring).

## Reading and resampling
- GDAL `/vsicurl/` is used through rasterio, with `GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN=EMPTY_DIR`, `CPL_VSIL_CURL_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS=.tif,.TIF,.tiff`, `GDAL_HTTP_MULTIPLEX=YES`, `GDAL_HTTP_MERGE_CONSECUTIVE_RANGES=YES` and retries.
- Per tile:
  - A probe opens the tile to get its bounds and overviews.
  - The recipe chooses the largest overview whose resolution is no coarser than the spacing, then `rasterio.open(path, overview_level=k)`.
  - It warps with `WarpedVRT` to the local CRS and grid, using average when downsampling and bilinear otherwise, with source nodata excluded.
  - It reads only the overlapped window and skips a tile if its window is already fully filled.
  - The first valid tile wins.
- Terrarium: tiles are fetched with 8 threads, mosaicked in EPSG:3857, and warped with `rasterio.warp.reproject`.

## Byte counting
It parses GDAL "VSICURL: Downloading a-b" debug lines through the `rasterio._err` logger and adds requests/apsw bytes. It needs `CPL_DEBUG=ON` inside `rasterio.Env`; output is not printed. It counts range bytes, so it is approximate.

## Timings and bytes (this sandbox, behind a proxy; includes FESM when 3dep_1m is used)
| Case | Time | Downloaded |
|---|---|---|
| FESM query alone | about 2 s | 2.5 MB |
| Test area 4.14 x 2.89 km @ 2 m, 3dep_1m | 2.6 to 4.5 s warm, 11 s first run | 12.7 to 14.7 MB |
| Test area @ 1 m (2889 x 4142 cells) | 8.1 s | 36.8 MB |
| Test area @ 5 m, with overview | 2.2 s | 8.3 MB |
| Test area @ 5 m, full-res averaging | 4.8 s | 36.5 MB |
| Test area @ 10 m / @ 30 m | 1.9 s / 1.5 s | 4.7 MB / 3.5 MB |
| 3dep_13 (2 m grid) | 0.8 to 1.2 s | 1.5 MB |
| cop30 (2 m grid) | about 2 s | 1.3 MB |
| terrarium (2 m grid) | about 1.2 s | 3.5 MB |
| 13.3 x 11.1 km @ 5 m, 3dep_1m, 6 tiles | 9.8 s | 47 MB |
| 16.7 x 11.1 km @ 5 m across the UTM 15/16 boundary | 15.5 s | 60 MB |

Compressed float overviews cost about 4 to 5 bytes per output cell, so budget about 5 MB per million cells, plus about 2.5 MB for FESM.

## Gotchas
- `rasterio.Env(GDAL_CACHEMAX="512")` raises "TypeError: an integer is required". Pass the int 512.
- The 3dep_13 and 3dep_1m tiles are huge (415 MB and 290 MB), so never download whole files. Always window or use overviews.
- Terrarium has no nodata and is mixed-source. The 3dep_13 and 3dep_1m rows are labelled bare earth, while cop30 includes tree and building height.
- 3DEP 1 m is NaN over open water outside the lidar footprint (Galveston, 70% valid). Water inside projects is hydro-flattened.
- The FESM query returns project footprints, not tile footprints, so tile existence is checked against the link lists.
- Because FESM is updated frequently, the 1.9 GB file's ETag and size change. The apsw VFS reads it fresh every time.
- The TNM API was not tested (blocked here). It should work from the user's PC, but it is not needed.
